sourceIssues.printed: "Lemma 1.1. The group scheme Num_{X/k} is constant if and only if there is an integer d ≥ 0 with the following property: For every invertible sheaf L on X̄ there is a numerically trivial invertible sheaf N on X̄ such that L^{⊗d} ⊗ N is the pullback of some invertible sheaf on X."
sourceIssues.reason: With d = 0 the property holds trivially (take N = O), so the "if" direction would fail: P¹_C, viewed as a proper R-scheme, has X̄ = P¹_C ⊔ P¹_C with Num = Z² and complex conjugation exchanging the two factors, so Num_{X/R} is not constant. Noted by the extraction (item 2).

sourceIssues.printed: "Proposition 3.1. Suppose the ground field k = F_q is finite and that the group scheme Num_{S/k} is constant. Then Γ(S_ā) → Γ(S_a) is a graph isomorphism respecting edge labels, and the implications (i)⇒(ii)⇔(iii) hold among the following three conditions: (i) The geometric fiber S_ā is reducible. (ii) The closed point a ∈ B is a rational point. (iii) The irreducible components of the schematic fiber S_a are birational to P¹."
sourceIssues.correction: (ii)⇔(iii) requires the geometric fiber to be singular (as in the applications, e.g. Proposition 3.2, which assumes C_red singular).
sourceIssues.reason: For S = E × P¹ → P¹ over F_q with E an elliptic curve, Num_{S/k} is constant, but the fiber over a rational point a is the smooth elliptic curve E, which is not birational to P¹: (ii) holds and (iii) fails. Noted by the extraction (item 14).

sourceIssues.printed: "Each triple (L, a, b) where L is an invertible R-module and a ∈ L, b ∈ L^{⊗−1} are elements with a ⊗ b = 2R yields a finite flat group scheme G^L_{a,b}, characterized by G^L_{a,b}(A) = {f ∈ L ⊗_R A | f^{⊗2} = a ⊗ f}, with group law f_1 ⋆ f_2 = f_1 + f_2 + b ⊗ f_1 ⊗ f_2."
sourceIssues.correction: f_1 ⋆ f_2 = f_1 + f_2 − b ⊗ f_1 ⊗ f_2, as in Oort–Tate.
sourceIssues.reason: With L = R = Z, a = 1, b = 2 (the constant group Z/2Z, as the text says next) and f_1 = f_2 = 1, the printed law gives 4, and 4² ≠ 1·4, so it is not in G; the minus sign gives 0, the group law of {0, 1}. For a = 2, b = 1 (μ₂) the minus sign matches (1 − f)(1 − g) = 1 − (f + g − fg). Noted by the extraction (item 51).

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Proposition 5.5, p.16, in arXiv 2004.07025v3 (9 August 2022, SHA-256 ae6481f2…6d61), whose text after the first page agrees with the author's third revised version of 19 July 2022 (the journal's revision date); the typeset Annals text (197 (2023), 1–63) was not obtained
sourceIssues.printed: "One the other hand, using Hensel's Lemma, any F_2^alg-valued point for Y → S can be extended to an A-valued point. Again with Proposition 5.4 we conclude that a family of canonical covering X ⊗ A → Y ⊗ A exists, whence X_F has good reduction over A, contradiction." (Here X_F is the generic fiber of the canonical covering constructed over Z[1/2], and A = W(F_2^sep), F = Frac A.)
sourceIssues.correction: Compare the two covers: over F they are canonical covers of the same Enriques surface and may differ by a twist by a class in H¹(F, μ₂) = F^×/F^{×2}. One way to close the gap: construct the local cover over Z₂ (using a Z₂-point, which exists since #Y(F₂) = 25 by Corollary 7.3), write the difference over Q₂ as (−1)^e 2^a 5^b, remove (−1)^e 2^a by twisting the Z[1/2]-cover by the étale torsor s² = (−1)^e 2^a, and 5^b by twisting the local cover by the unramified torsor Z₂[z]/(z² − z − 1); then both covers agree over Q₂ and give a smooth proper model everywhere, contradicting Fontaine.
sourceIssues.reason: Canonical coverings are unique only up to such twists, so good reduction of the local cover over A does not by itself give good reduction of X_F. The extraction supplies the four-twist repair sketched in the correction (report, "Four-twist repair"). The main theorem is not in doubt.

sourceIssues.printed: "If r ≥ 2, we actually have C_i ≃ P¹, and the canonical map Γ(C̄) → Γ(C) is a graph isomorphism respecting edge labels, again by Proposition 3.1. Choose a component C_i corresponding to a terminal vertex of Γ(C). Then there is exactly one component C_j intersecting C_i, which has (C_i · C_j) ≤ 2. In turn, from the three rational points in C_i = P¹ at least one is contained in the regular locus of C_red."
sourceIssues.correction: For multiplicative fibers I_r with r ≥ 3 the dual graph is a cycle and has no terminal vertex; take any rational component, which meets the others in two points, and use the third point of P¹(F₂). For additive fibers, whose dual graph is a tree, choose a terminal component of multiplicity one.
sourceIssues.reason: The argument as written applies a terminal-vertex choice to every fiber type, which fails for cycles. The conclusion still holds by the modified choice. Noted by the extraction (report §"Source precision", item 11).

sourceIssues.printed: "According to the definition of Mordell–Weil groups we have MW(J/P¹) = J(F) = Pic⁰_{Y_F/F}(F) = Pic⁰(Y_F), where F is the function field of the projective line. The latter equality holds because Br(F) = 0, by Tsen's Theorem."
sourceIssues.correction: Here k = F₂, so F = F₂(t) and Br(F) ≠ 0: Tsen's theorem applies to function fields over algebraically closed fields. The equality Pic⁰_{Y_F/F}(F) = Pic⁰(Y_F) needs another argument, for instance passing to F_2^alg(t), where Tsen applies, and taking Galois invariants of the geometric Picard group.
sourceIssues.reason: A concrete nonzero class: the cyclic algebra (F₄(t)/F₂(t), t), since norms from F₄(t) have even valuation at t = 0, so t is not a norm. Noted by the extraction (item 94), which proposes the repair.

sourceIssues.printed: "Indeed, a fiber J_x is unstable if and only if c_4 ∈ F₂[T] vanishes at the point x ([14], Proposition 5.1), and in our situation c_4 = a_1^4 with deg(a_1) ≤ 1."
sourceIssues.correction: A fiber is unstable (additive) if and only if Δ and c_4 both vanish at x; c_4(x) = 0 alone also holds for a smooth supersingular fiber.
sourceIssues.reason: In characteristic 2, c_4 = a_1^4 vanishes at x exactly when the reduction is supersingular or additive. The argument only uses "unstable ⇒ c_4(x) = 0", which is true, to conclude that there is at most one unstable fiber, so nothing downstream changes. Noted by the extraction (report item 8).
